finding: Historical proposal that a giant impact formed the hemispheric contrast.
dichotomy_use: Establishes the northern-impact hypothesis to test.
limitation: Title and bibliographic record checked; original argument still needs full-text review.

finding: Tests whether an impactor population can account for the lowlands and other large basins.
dichotomy_use: Requires an impact origin to fit basin statistics as well as hemisphere shape.
limitation: Results depend on the adopted impactor size distribution and recognition of old basins.

finding: Compares endogenous, single-impact and multiple-impact explanations against geological constraints.
dichotomy_use: Useful framework for asking which observations each mechanism actually explains.
limitation: A historical assessment predating modern gravity, radar and seismic datasets.

finding: Reviews the geological, topographic and tectonic expressions of the dichotomy.
dichotomy_use: Separates formation of the contrast from subsequent modification of the boundary.
limitation: Review predates InSight; old model parameters require updating.

finding: Removing the inferred Tharsis contribution reveals an elliptical boundary compatible with an oblique impact.
dichotomy_use: Tests northern-basin geometry using gravity and topography together.
limitation: The reconstructed ellipse depends on separating volcanic loading and crustal structure.

finding: Three-dimensional impact simulations produce a large elliptical northern excavation within a restricted impact parameter range.
dichotomy_use: Supplies quantitative northern-impact initial conditions.
limitation: Success depends on material physics, melt treatment and the assumed initial crust.

finding: Large-impact calculations explore crustal removal, melting and disruption as a route to the dichotomy.
dichotomy_use: Connects basin formation to crustal and magnetic consequences.
limitation: A simplified impact geometry cannot independently establish the actual impact trajectory.

finding: Proposes that mantle convection and the dichotomy are dynamically linked.
dichotomy_use: Foundational reference for degree-one convection.
limitation: Metadata and primary-source preview checked; detailed model assumptions remain to be extracted.

finding: Layered mantle viscosity permits degree-one convection to develop much faster than in some phase-change models.
dichotomy_use: Makes formation timescale and viscosity contrast explicit tests of an internal origin.
limitation: The appropriate early Martian rheology is uncertain; a simulated pattern is not an observation.

finding: Studies a hybrid impact-driven degree-one convection scenario.
dichotomy_use: Prevents treating impacts and convection as mutually exclusive explanations.
limitation: Bibliographic record and primary preview checked; quantitative outcomes require full-text extraction.

finding: Strength-inclusive impact models with crust production favour a southern impact in their explored parameter space.
dichotomy_use: Challenges the assumption that an impact must excavate the northern hemisphere.
limitation: Preferred impact sizes and geometry depend on melting, strength and crust-production prescriptions.

finding: Coupled impact and long-term mantle models build thicker crust on the impacted southern hemisphere.
dichotomy_use: Tests an impact followed by geological evolution rather than an instantaneous crater alone.
limitation: Model preference is conditional on impact parameters and mantle viscosity; data are available on request.

finding: Crustal insulation and melt extraction can amplify a long-wavelength crustal thickness perturbation.
dichotomy_use: Offers a feedback mechanism that can enlarge an initially small asymmetry.
limitation: Parameterized thermal models do not establish the origin or uniqueness of the initial perturbation.

finding: Boundary stratigraphy and structure distinguish an ancient dichotomy from younger erosion and faulting.
dichotomy_use: Prevents dating primordial formation from the age of young boundary landforms.
limitation: Regional exposures and resurfacing limit extrapolation around the entire planet.

finding: Proposes northern crustal recycling and spreading, with testable structural and gravity predictions.
dichotomy_use: Retains early plate tectonics as a historical alternative to impact and stagnant-lid convection.
limitation: Proposed tectonic reconstructions are interpretations, not confirmed Martian plate boundaries.

finding: InSight seismic observations constrain crustal layering and thickness beneath the lander.
dichotomy_use: Provides the local anchor for global gravity-based crustal models.
limitation: Bibliographic record and editorial summary checked; original inversion and alternatives need detailed review.

finding: Combines the InSight crustal anchor with gravity and topography to generate global crustal models.
dichotomy_use: Quantifies how much hemispheric contrast must be explained by crustal thickness and density.
limitation: Absolute thickness is strongly conditional on the adopted seismic layering and crustal density.

finding: Multi-orbit surface waves constrain average crustal thickness and limit large north–south density contrasts in the tested models.
dichotomy_use: Adds constraints beyond the immediate InSight column.
limitation: Path coverage and the tested structural parameterization remain important; models share underlying datasets.

finding: Joint inversion of marsquake and geophysical information admits alternative thermal and crustal structures.
dichotomy_use: Tests compatibility between seismic structure and global geophysical constraints.
limitation: Event locations, temperature and structure trade off; this is not a second global seismic network.

finding: Different attenuation inferred along Terra Cimmeria and Cerberus paths is interpreted as a thermal contrast.
dichotomy_use: Provides a potential mantle-related expression of the dichotomy.
limitation: Limited paths, scattering and source effects complicate temperature inference; present contrast does not uniquely date its cause.

finding: Orbiter tracking reveals asymmetric seasonal tidal gravity; inversion supports a hotter southern mantle.
dichotomy_use: Adds a present-day interior constraint; atmospheric pressure loading is explicitly modelled with MCD.
limitation: Convection and crustal insulation remain alternatives. Atmospheric and elastic-model sensitivity must accompany the inversion.

finding: Initial InSight reflected-wave analysis supported a large liquid core.
dichotomy_use: Constrains thermal evolution and possible dynamo histories.
limitation: Later molten-layer interpretations revise the inferred core size; these estimates must not be averaged as independent measurements.

finding: An enriched molten silicate layer above a smaller liquid core reconciles seismic and geophysical constraints.
dichotomy_use: Changes the thermal boundary conditions for early dynamo and mantle evolution models.
limitation: Inversion depends on assumed composition and layer structure; a liquid layer alone does not imply an active dynamo.

finding: Seismic phases are interpreted as evidence for a roughly 600-km-radius solid inner core.
dichotomy_use: Requires testing present-day interior models separately from early full-sphere dynamo models.
limitation: Phase identification and inversion assumptions matter. Consult the linked author correction before reuse.

finding: Corrects a Methods citation for the effect of light elements on liquid-core properties.
dichotomy_use: Keeps the inner-core source trail current.
limitation: The notice corrects a reference, not the reported inner-core radius; it is not a separate independent result.

finding: Orbital tracking analysis provides a constraint on the contrast in bulk crustal density between hemispheres.
dichotomy_use: Helps distinguish a thickness contrast from a density contrast.
limitation: Numerical densities were not reliably preserved in harvested abstract equations; consult the original figures before quantitative reuse.

finding: Thermal models explore differentiation and partial melting of the thick southern crust.
dichotomy_use: Connects heat-producing elements, crust thickness and lithological diversity.
limitation: Conditional petrological and thermal calculations do not map observed melt throughout the south.

finding: Two-hemisphere thermal models connect crustal thickness and radiogenic enrichment to different lithospheric temperatures and elastic thicknesses.
dichotomy_use: Provides a thermal benchmark for testing magnetic acquisition and retention in the same crustal histories.
limitation: Sections 5.5, 5.6 and 6 consulted. Polar elastic thickness need not represent an entire hemisphere; a well-mixed mantle and parameterized columns omit spatial dynamics.

finding: Seismic and petrological modelling interprets a lower-crustal layer beneath InSight as melt-depleted ultramafic material.
dichotomy_use: Adds lithological differentiation without requiring plate tectonics.
limitation: A local seismic anchor and phase-equilibrium models do not establish global lower-crustal uniformity.

finding: Mars Global Surveyor measurements reveal strong, spatially heterogeneous crustal remanent fields.
dichotomy_use: Establishes magnetization as a major constraint on early crustal evolution.
limitation: Weak fields above basins are not a unique clock for dynamo cessation.

finding: Alternating, elongated magnetic anomalies were interpreted in relation to ancient tectonic processes.
dichotomy_use: Tests whether magnetic spatial organization contains evidence of crustal mobility.
limitation: Orbital stripes alone do not demonstrate seafloor spreading or Earth-like plate tectonics.

finding: Combines MGS and MAVEN observations into a global spherical-harmonic crustal-field model.
dichotomy_use: Provides a reproducible field layer for comparison with geology and crustal thickness.
limitation: Altitude and spatial bandwidth filter the signal; downward continuation is not direct surface measurement.

finding: Reports crustal and time-varying magnetic fields measured at the InSight landing site.
dichotomy_use: Links a ground measurement to the orbital magnetic picture.
limitation: Metadata checked; detailed separation of external and crustal fields needs full-text extraction.

finding: Zhurong measurements reveal weak local crustal fields along a traverse in Utopia Planitia.
dichotomy_use: Adds a rare northern ground constraint independent of orbital altitude smoothing.
limitation: A short traverse is not representative of the entire northern hemisphere; local demagnetization is an alternative.

finding: Magnetic signals associated with ancient and younger terrains are interpreted as evidence of early and prolonged dynamo activity.
dichotomy_use: Challenges a single shutdown date inferred only from weakly magnetized large basins.
limitation: Geological ages and the depths and histories of magnetic sources remain uncertain.

finding: Cooling and polarity reversals can suppress orbital anomalies above impact basins despite an active dynamo.
dichotomy_use: Tests whether weak basin magnetism actually requires post-dynamo formation.
limitation: The explored basin-size range is much smaller than Borealis; a direct extrapolation is not validated.

finding: Hemispheric core heat-flow forcing can produce a strongly asymmetric dynamo.
dichotomy_use: Offers a source-field alternative to selective destruction of crustal magnetization.
limitation: Requires compatible core–mantle thermal forcing and preservation of the resulting crustal record.

finding: Explores hemispherical magnetic-field generation in dynamo models without an inner core.
dichotomy_use: Tests how early core geometry affects asymmetric magnetism.
limitation: An early fully liquid core and a present solid inner core are different temporal hypotheses.

finding: Models impact-induced magnetic changes through excavation, heating and shock.
dichotomy_use: Helps distinguish field absence from destruction or removal of magnetic carriers.
limitation: Mineralogy and impact physics alter demagnetization efficiency; simplified field histories are conditional.

finding: Compositional variations are investigated as a contributor to strong regional crustal magnetic anomalies.
dichotomy_use: Introduces carrier abundance alongside dynamo intensity and thermal history.
limitation: Surface spectra sample different depths from orbital magnetic sources; correlation does not fix causality.

finding: Reviews the gap between orbital, surface and sample-scale magnetic observations.
dichotomy_use: Organizes the scale mismatch that a joint dichotomy study must address.
limitation: A review supplies synthesis rather than an independent measurement for model scoring.

finding: Micromagnetic observations in ALH 84001 are interpreted as records of ancient polarity reversals.
dichotomy_use: Constrains ancient field behaviour during impact-heating episodes.
limitation: Age assignment, magnetic carriers and resetting histories must be evaluated before inferring dynamo duration.

finding: ALH 84001 paleointensity work supports a substantial ancient Martian magnetic field.
dichotomy_use: Supplies a sample-scale constraint complementary to orbital remanent anomalies.
limitation: Uncertain acquisition history and unknown original location prevent a direct hemispheric map.

finding: ALH 84001 carbonate-related remanence is investigated as an ancient paleofield recorder.
dichotomy_use: Links mineral formation, low-temperature history and early magnetism.
limitation: Mineral-scale recording and later overprints must be separated; meteorite crystallization age is not automatically magnetic age.

finding: Martian meteorite families contain different magnetic carriers, including titanomagnetite and pyrrhotite.
dichotomy_use: Shows why magnetization cannot be interpreted solely as field intensity.
limitation: The measured meteorite collection is lithologically and statistically biased.

finding: NWA 7034 contains abundant magnetic oxides capable of carrying strong crustal remanence.
dichotomy_use: Provides a candidate lithological analogue for strong Martian anomalies.
limitation: Rock-magnetic capacity remains informative even when natural remanence is terrestrially contaminated; the two must not be conflated.

finding: Experiments and nine paired NWA 7034 stones demonstrate destructive remagnetization by collectors' hand magnets.
dichotomy_use: Makes collection history a mandatory quality field in any meteorite paleofield synthesis.
limitation: The studied stones cannot provide pristine Martian paleointensity; this does not negate all mineralogical information or every future sample.

finding: Tissint records a weak post-shock field interpreted as a local Martian crustal field.
dichotomy_use: Demonstrates magnetic recording long after the early dynamo interval.
limitation: A young weak paleofield need not imply a young global dynamo.

finding: Oriented subsamples of MIL 03346 preserve a tested remanence and an approximately 5-microtesla paleointensity.
dichotomy_use: Provides a nakhlite constraint with explicit laboratory preservation tests.
limitation: The signal can be explained by older magnetized crust; mutually oriented subsamples do not recover absolute Martian orientation.

finding: Reviews how geologically contextualized, oriented returned samples could resolve magnetic history and thermal or aqueous alteration.
dichotomy_use: Identifies missing ages, orientations and source lithologies in the current evidence.
limitation: Existing meteorites are sparse and commonly reset. Proposed sample-return science is not an accomplished laboratory measurement.

finding: Perseverance observations identify potential iron-oxide magnetic carriers in igneous rocks.
dichotomy_use: Helps prioritize contextualized samples for future rock-magnetic work.
limitation: Spectral identification of possible carriers is not a direct ancient paleofield measurement.

finding: Reviews Martian meteorite petrology, isotopes, ages and sampling biases.
dichotomy_use: Provides the geochemical context needed to interpret magnetic results and mantle reservoirs.
limitation: Meteorite names, pairing groups and launch events are not equivalent independent samples.

finding: Multiple chronometers constrain ancient near-surface material and later heterogeneous heating in the NWA 7034 source terrain.
dichotomy_use: Conditional survival and burial constraints can test event sequences predicted by dichotomy origin models.
limitation: Dichotomy-age discussion consulted. Local provenance, burial and thermal assumptions prevent a universal formation date; crystallization and later metamorphism are distinct.

finding: Ancient zircon ages and hafnium isotopes imply very early extraction and subsequent reworking of a primordial crust.
dichotomy_use: Constrains how quickly initial crustal reservoirs formed.
limitation: Reservoir model ages differ from measured crystallization ages and do not directly date the hemispheric boundary.

finding: Crater and terrain analysis identifies a candidate ejection site for the NWA 7034 family in the southern highlands.
dichotomy_use: Offers a route from meteorite laboratory data to geological context.
limitation: Provenance is inferred, with multiple excavation and reworking episodes; it is not a known collection coordinate on Mars.

finding: Links groups of Martian meteorites to candidate source craters through ejection and geological modelling.
dichotomy_use: Allows explicit provenance hypotheses for comparing meteorites with mapped provinces.
limitation: Meteorites from the same launch group must not be counted as independent regional observations.

finding: Shock microstructures in ancient zircon record a high-pressure impact after zircon formation.
dichotomy_use: Tests early bombardment histories and preservation of primordial crust.
limitation: An old grain age alone does not date the later shock event.

finding: Nanometre-scale mineral and chemical evidence in ancient zircon is interpreted as early hydrothermal activity.
dichotomy_use: Links water–rock interaction to early crustal modification and possible magnetic carriers.
limitation: A local grain-scale environment does not establish a planet-wide ocean or magnetic field.

finding: Experiments explore buoyant differentiated protocrust formation during oxidized magma-ocean crystallization.
dichotomy_use: Expands possible initial crustal compositions for dichotomy models.
limitation: Laboratory conditions and extrapolation to a global magma ocean are model assumptions, not direct mapping of Mars.

finding: Erosional remnants near the dichotomy boundary indicate substantial removal of ancient highland material.
dichotomy_use: Separates retreat of the visible boundary from the original crustal boundary.
limitation: Regional erosion does not by itself explain the initial hemispheric crustal contrast.

finding: Orbital observations document diverse clay-bearing terrains along the dichotomy region.
dichotomy_use: Tests heterogeneous alteration histories and substrate composition.
limitation: Spectral exposure, dust and observational coverage bias comparisons between hemispheres.

finding: Geological mapping reconstructs volcanic, tectonic and aqueous modifications in southern Utopia.
dichotomy_use: Provides a regional northern-lowland case study for separating formation from resurfacing.
limitation: Regional stratigraphic interpretations cannot be generalized to all northern plains.

finding: Delta elevations in the examined region are consistent with local closed-basin lakes rather than one ocean level.
dichotomy_use: Tests shoreline interpretations used to reconstruct later northern hydrology.
limitation: The regional result does not exclude every proposed Martian ocean at every epoch.

finding: Hydrogen-isotope measurements in meteorites constrain model histories of Martian water loss and storage.
dichotomy_use: Connects atmospheric evolution with crustal water reservoirs.
limitation: Inferred inventories depend on fractionation and reservoir-exchange assumptions; they do not identify the dichotomy-forming mechanism.

finding: Plasma simulations show that a weak intrinsic dipole can increase ion escape under the tested conditions.
dichotomy_use: Challenges a simple field-off, atmosphere-lost causal chain.
limitation: The dependence varies with field strength and solar conditions; present-day simulations are not a complete early-Mars loss history.

finding: Models ejecta burial and heating of the southern crust and considers a convection-based origin for magnetic lineations.
dichotomy_use: Prior work directly connects dichotomy formation scenarios to magnetic survival; any new consistency test must engage with it.
limitation: Discussion and conclusion consulted. Uniform ejecta and assumed thermal/recording histories restrict generality; later reacquisition must also be considered.

finding: Early geotherms inferred for Terra Cimmeria are used to evaluate candidate magnetic carriers and magnetized depths.
dichotomy_use: Establishes prior thermal-carrier consistency tests that a modern joint analysis should extend rather than claim to invent.
limitation: Abstract consulted with limited section previews. Inferred heat flow, loading age and source depths are conditional; Curie depth is not a directly measured magnetic boundary.

finding: Numerical hemispherical dynamos driven by imposed core-mantle boundary heat-flux variations can reverse rapidly.
dichotomy_use: A hemispheric field explanation must satisfy time-integrated magnetic recording as well as spatial field contrast.
limitation: Author-hosted abstract consulted. The reported reversal problem concerns this simulated regime, not every possible Martian dynamo.

finding: Localized magnetic spectra are interpreted as different equivalent source depths in northern lowlands and southern highlands.
dichotomy_use: Depth estimates offer a target for joint thermal and magnetic history tests.
limitation: Abstract consulted. Source geometry and spectral localization affect equivalent depths; these estimates reuse the Langlais field model and are not independent observations of layer boundaries.
